learningObjective: Identify the kernel-support requirements for KV cache quantization to be effective for both memory and bandwidth savings.

canonicalClaims.claim: KV cache quantization saves memory footprint whenever KVs are stored quantized; to also save memory bandwidth in attention, either the attention kernel must dequant-in-register on the fly (INT8/FP8 KV, FP16 attention math) or natively consume quantized KVs (FP8 attention on Hopper, INT8 attention kernels).
conditions: The framework and attention kernel support the chosen KV precision.
Per-token / per-head-per-token scale granularity is used to preserve accuracy.
nonImplications: Does not imply eager dequantization to FP16 before attention preserves bandwidth benefits.
Does not imply KV precision must equal weight precision.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache quantization requires model weights to be quantized to the same precision.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Mixed-precision (FP16 weights + INT8 KV cache, or BF16 weights + FP8 KV) is standard in production stacks.

misconceptions.claim: Eager dequant to FP16 before attention preserves the bandwidth savings of KV quantization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Once dequantized to FP16, the same FP16-sized buffer is read by attention — bandwidth savings vanish.

misconceptions.claim: The attention kernel must use a single scale per head across all context positions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-token (or per-block-per-token) scaling is the norm and delivers better accuracy; kernels handle per-token scales via inline loading.

misconceptions.claim: Dequant-in-register overhead makes INT8 KV attention slower than FP16 KV attention.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dequant adds a small number of ops per KV load; the HBM traffic reduction usually dominates, making INT8 KV attention faster in bandwidth-bound regimes.

implementationFacts: TensorRT-LLM provides `--kv_cache_dtype int8` and `--kv_cache_dtype fp8` options.
FlashAttention-3 supports native FP8 attention on Hopper.
vLLM PagedAttention adapts block sizes to the KV dtype.
performanceScenarios: LLaMA-70B at 8K context on H100: FP8 KV reduces attention memory bandwidth by ~2× vs FP16, delivering ~1.8× decode speedup at high concurrency.
